claims.statement: The derivative residue is 7+4*(-1)^floor(n/2); the period-four sign is the quadratic refinement (-1)^(n(n-1)/2), Walsh upper-bit character and Clifford reversion grade sign. The carry mask uses the shifted conjugation sign.
claims.domain: Integer n for residue identities; nonnegative grades for the Clifford interpretation.
claims.hypotheses: Original four-pole forcing for the derivative assertion.
claims.quantifiers: Every integer index in the algebraic identities.
claims.boundary: A modular derivative representative is not a real derivative; source time and carry index differ.

claims.statement: A uniform root is a maximum law and a norm-ball radial law; radius sqrt(U), ratio V and a fair orientation construct two independent uniforms pathwise.
claims.domain: Independent uniforms on (0,1); finite dimensional norm balls with normalized Lebesgue measure.
claims.hypotheses: Declared volume measure and independence of the construction inputs.
claims.quantifiers: Every radius in [0,1]; any finite dimension d>=1.
claims.boundary: A radial law does not specify an ordered pair or full vector law.
claims.next_falsifier: Marginal, Jacobian or CDF failure under the explicit construction.

claims.statement: The aligned antisymmetric Haar density preserves every symmetric pair observable law while changing the ordered carry response; its stationary Markov mode rotates by i*epsilon and realizes the period-four sign in lag correlations.
claims.hypotheses: Explicit kernel 1+epsilon*(a tensor c-c tensor a), uniform stationary start.
claims.quantifiers: All bounded measurable symmetric observables and all nonnegative lags.
claims.boundary: A diagnostic probability model, not the law of the BBP source.
claims.next_falsifier: Failure of positivity, stationarity, a declared phase sign, or the orthogonal-wedge mutation.

claims.statement: Under uniform marginals and max CDF r^2, the selected difference-quarter gate has sharp range [1/16,7/8]. Explicit continuous densities attain both endpoints.
claims.domain: All joint probability laws on [0,1)^2 satisfying the hypotheses.
claims.hypotheses: Both marginals uniform and P(max(X,Y)<r)=r^2 for every r in [0,1].
claims.quantifiers: Universal over such laws; existence of absolutely continuous extremizers and all convex-mixture values.
claims.boundary: Removing the cofactor marginal allows a full-maximum-law zero-hit example.
claims.next_falsifier: A failed cell inequality or marginal/diagonal polynomial in an extremizer.

claims.statement: For every finite source shell, selected frequency d_B>=F1_B+c1_B-F2_B. An eventual positive lower bound on that three-mass statistic implies the open selected carry-density target.
claims.domain: Authentic U_0=0 four-pole recurrence, J=n mod4, K=[fractional(U_n)]_4 via dyadic rational reduction.
claims.hypotheses: Inherited exact source clock; eventual three-mass premise only for the asymptotic consequence.
claims.quantifiers: Finite inequality for every integer B>=1; target requires every sufficiently large integer B.
claims.boundary: No eventual source estimate has been proved. The implication does not prove full normality.
claims.next_falsifier: Source-specific violation of a proposed error budget or a hidden replacement of K by a uniform sample.

claims.statement: The four original poles equal five positive Beta(k,2) volumes; normalized branches have two-uniform product/two-exponential-sum constructions. Two branches of valuation -1 must combine to restore an odd denominator.
claims.domain: Original n>=1; real k>0 for the probability construction.
claims.quantifiers: All n>=1 and all declared branch parameters.
claims.boundary: The +2 Gamma argument differs from arithmetic time advance +8. Auxiliary draws do not supply an orbit coupling.
claims.next_falsifier: Pole-coefficient mutation, denominator-valuation error, or an invalid integral interchange.

claims.statement: The actual period-four gate has Laplace transform 1/(2t cosh t); its exponential-probe Mellin response is Gamma(s)*DirichletBeta(s) and its s=1 scale integral is pi/4.
claims.domain: x>=0, real t>0; complex s with Re(s)>0.
claims.hypotheses: Declared right-continuous floor gate and exponential probe law.
claims.boundary: This is a universal mask response, not empirical BBP sampling. Dirichlet beta has odd character parity.
claims.next_falsifier: Shifted-gate mutation, convergence-domain violation, or wrong character parity.
